newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr, TWI end lower after March qtr jobs data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr, TWI end lower after March qtr jobs data.

text.p: Weaker-than-expected jobs data for the March quarter took the New Zealand dollar sharply lower on Tuesday and the short term outlook was for more downside.
By 0515 GMT the Kiwi was finishing on its lows at US$0.6863/70 from its 0.6889/96 open, having traded a 0.6866-95 range.
The Trade-Weighted Index was also sharply lower, closing at at 68.19 from 68.51.
Statistics New Zealand said earlier that unemployment had risen to 6.4 percent in the March quarter from 5.9 percent in December. Seasonally adjusted employment fell by 0.1 percent.
When the number came out, exporter buying around US$0.6880 supported the Kiwi briefly.
"Once that was soaked up, along with a little overseas buying, it just drifted to the day's low on that number," said one dealer.
"Over the next 24 hours we would expect a test of lower levels," he said. A test of 0.6850 was likely in the short term and the currency was likely to remain offered around 0.6885.
"Once the offshore markets have a look at those numbers and see that the economy is in a slowing down process, they are probably likely to sell the Kiwi as well," he said.
